statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk 3% (low) with no Nasdaq-100 price path observable inside the CME weekend halt, against Stress of 68% (high) as OPEC+ formally holds November output steady while the Riyadh facility fire and a Hormuz tanker strike remain unconfirmed in supply terms.
recommendation: Tail remains far below the block threshold, so the mapped policy state stays EA_ON. A narrow danger window is published across the 22:00Z CME reopen and the hour after it, 00:00-02:00 Berlin on 5 October, where the published forecast Tail path reaches the WATCH band on gap and discontinuity risk rather than on observed structure.
headline: OPEC+ confirms November quotas in an official statement, resolving the weekend's last unpriced supply checkpoint, while a Hormuz tanker strike and an unconfirmed Riyadh fire keep Stress high and the CME halt holds Tail at its floor
body:
CME equity-index futures have been halted since Friday 21:00Z and reopen at 22:00Z on 4 October, so no Nasdaq-100 price path exists to assess and Tail stays at its structural floor of 3%. The last observed path was orderly two-way behaviour. The cash index traded to an all-time intraday high of 31,017.53 on Friday 2 October, fully retraced it, and finished at a record 30,807.93, up 1.00% from a 30,501.56 previous close, in the lower half of its 30,737.07-31,017.53 range. Nasdaq-100 futures settled roughly 0.9% higher and about 0.7% below their own session high, with VIX settling at 15.31, down 6.59%, after a 15.30-16.24 range. A record high that is fully retraced into the close is the opposite of the shallow-pullback, repeated-extension structure that Tail measures.

Stress is marked down a further notch to 68% from the 70% published an hour earlier, eleven points below the 79% ceiling reached at 09:00Z. The reason is specific rather than drift: the weekend's last unpriced supply checkpoint has now resolved formally rather than on sourced reporting. The seven core OPEC+ members, Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Algeria, Kazakhstan and Oman, issued a statement agreeing to maintain September 2026 required production for November 2026, a joint quota of 31 million barrels a day, extending the pause begun in October. The group completed unwinding 1.65 million bpd of 2023 voluntary cuts in September and keeps a further 2 million bpd of 2022 cuts in place to year-end; the next monthly review is 1 November.

Two weekend developments argue against easing Stress further. The Houthis claim a ballistic-missile and drone strike on an Aramco site in Riyadh, and fires were visible at a facility south of the capital on Saturday, but the Saudi-led coalition calls the account misleading and Aramco has not confirmed a cause, so no supply loss is established. Separately, UKMTO reported on Sunday that a tanker was struck by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz with engine-room damage. The strait has been effectively closed since 28 February 2026, so a single vessel strike is an incremental datapoint inside an existing regime rather than a new one. Brent is $102.25 and WTI $91.11.

The rate path is the clearest offset. September payrolls were soft enough to lift the unemployment rate to 4.2% from 4.1%, and CME FedWatch odds of an October 0.25% hike fell from 64.2% a week earlier to roughly 17-23%, with only about 0.22% of further tightening priced through end-2026. The 2 October H.15 release shows the 2-year at 4.78%, the 10-year at 5.24% and the 30-year at 5.61%, with the front end lower on the week. None of yields, VIX, oil or breadth is currently aligned in a way that would amplify a one-way index path.

Confidence is raised to 87%. Current index, volatility, yield and oil levels are verified against primary sources, the OPEC+ outcome is now an official statement rather than sourced reporting, the geopolitical items are verified in reputable current coverage, and the seven-day U.S. calendar is complete. The one material gap is unchanged and structural: the weekend halt means there is no live price path, which is why Tail is published as a floor rather than as a measurement. The shared Finviz context file was last collected on 29 September and reports partial collection, so it is stale under the 90-minute freshness rule and was not used.

lookbackSummary: Across the past 24 published hours Claude held Tail at 3% in every slot, while Stress bottomed at 52% at 14:00Z on 3 October and then ratcheted steadily to a 79% ceiling by 09:00Z on 4 October before easing to 73% at 10:00Z and 70% at 11:00Z as the weekend's open checkpoints began to resolve. Confidence stayed in the 83-86% band. Every hour mapped to EA_ON and green, and the dominant mode was normal throughout.
outlookSummary: The closed Sunday session carries no scoreable Nasdaq-100 structure, so Tail is held between 3% and 6% through 20:00Z while Stress is marked down to 68% on the formal OPEC+ November decision. Tail then steps to 10% in the final closed hour and is raised to 21% and 20%, inside the WATCH band, across the 22:00Z CME reopen and the hour after it, which together form the published danger window. It decays conditionally to 8% by 11:00Z on 5 October on the assumption that price discovery is orderly, an assumption that a reopen gap holding without meaningful retracement would invalidate. Confidence troughs at 78% at the reopen and recovers to 86% once a continuous path is observable again.

The last observed structure was orderly: Friday's record 31,017.53 intraday high was fully retraced into a 30,807.93 close. Stress eases to 68% as OPEC+ formally held November quotas.

NQ futures settled roughly 0.9% higher on Friday

Aramco has not confirmed the cause of the Riyadh facility fire

forecast.analysis: Closed hour; Tail 6% on reopen proximity alone. Stress ticks back to 67% because the two hours ahead carry gap risk against a weekend headline set that includes the Hormuz tanker strike and an explicit U.S. signal of a pending decision on Iran.

Weekend headline set not yet priced by any traded instrument

forecast.analysis: Final closed hour. Tail is raised to 10% as the published path approaches the discontinuity. A weekend gap is a single repricing event; the exposure that Tail measures is to what follows the gap, not to the gap itself. No structure is observable until 22:00Z.
drivers: Last hour before the 22:00Z CME reopen
A gap is a discontinuity, not yet a one-way path
Confidence steps to 81% with no live path available

forecast.analysis: Reopen hour, and the published Tail is lifted to 21%, inside the WATCH band. This is conditional gap and discontinuity risk at the first print after a two-day halt with unresolved Iran and Yemen headlines, not observed structure. A gap that then holds without retracement is the case to watch.
drivers: CME equity-index futures reopen at 22:00Z / 00:00 Berlin
Conditional gap risk from unpriced weekend Iran and Yemen news

forecast.analysis: Second hour of trade, Tail held at 20% and still in the WATCH band. The published assumption is that first-hour discovery is two-way; shallow pullbacks with repeated extension away from the open would be the amplifier this score is reserved for. Tokyo opens at the end of the hour.

forecast.analysis: Tail decays to 15% on the assumption that reopen discovery was orderly, and the published danger window closes at this slot. The assumption is explicit and falsifiable: repeated extension after failed retracements through the Asian handover would invalidate it and argue for a higher path.

Invalidation: repeated extension after failed retracements

drivers: Asian session liquidity builds as reopen positioning clears
A traded price restores the primary evidence channel
Conditional on two-way behaviour rather than one-way extension

forecast.analysis: Tail 12%. The hour carries no scheduled U.S. catalyst; the conditional path assumes the index trades around Friday's 30,807.93 cash reference, with the 31,017.53 record high acting as the nearest structural level rather than a level extended through without pullback.
drivers: No scheduled U.S. release inside this hour
Record 31,017.53 is the nearest reference level overhead

forecast.analysis: Tail 11%, Stress 65%. A mid-Asian hour with the index's own path as the only live evidence. The published decay assumes realised volatility continues to behave like Friday's 15.31 VIX close rather than repricing on an overnight Middle East headline.

forecast.analysis: Tail 10% as the conditional path flattens. Cross-asset alignment is assumed to stay loose: a 5.24% 10-year and $102.25 Brent are already-known, already-absorbed levels rather than fresh amplifiers acting on the index in this hour.

forecast.analysis: Tail 8%. The next hard checkpoint sits outside this window: S&P Global services and composite finals at 13:45Z and ISM Services at 14:00Z on 5 October. Until then the conditional path is shallow and driven by the index's own structure.
